question: A 55-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 2-month history of headaches, facial numbness, recurrent epistaxis, and a 5-kg (11-lb) weight loss. He recently immigrated from Hong Kong. Examination shows right-sided cervical lymphadenopathy. Endoscopy shows an exophytic nasopharyngeal mass. Histologic examination of a biopsy specimen of the mass shows sheets of undifferentiated cells with nuclear pleomorphism and abundant mitotic figures. The patient most likely acquired the causal pathogen of his nasopharyngeal mass via which of the following routes of transmission?
